screens.name: landing
strengths: “Let’s get oddly specific” gives the experience a memorable, characterful opening.
The shard mirror and violet CTA establish a coherent visual identity immediately.
problems: The headline’s reflected lettering sits behind the description and looks like rendering residue. Remove the text reflection; keep reflections on the mirror.
The description, CTA footnote and how-it-works tile compete to explain the game. Shorten the description to two lines and consolidate the repeated card-and-guess counts beneath the CTA.

screens.name: lobby
strengths: Three large choices make the voice setting easy to understand and tap.
The lavender, pink and neutral orbs give the options distinct emotional tones.
problems: “Make it fun” looks selected, but the screen provides no explicit continuation control. Add a compact Continue button beneath the choices and a checkmark to the selected option.
Italic descriptions make all three choices feel like decorative quotations. Use upright sans-serif descriptions at 16px and reduce each option’s vertical padding by 8px.

screens.name: chapter intro
strengths: The floating phone island makes the chapter feel like a place rather than a questionnaire section.
The mirror thumbnail connects chapter progress to the central shard mechanic.
problems: The artwork consumes almost a third of the viewport before the chapter title appears. Reduce its height by roughly 50px and move the title upward.
“0 of 40 shards. Each answer adds one” breaks into an awkward headline-and-fragment construction. Change it to “0 / 40 shards collected” with “Each answer adds one” as a separate caption.

screens.name: scenario card
strengths: The scenario is specific, funny and immediately imaginable.
Large answer surfaces and consistent alignment make the response choices easy to scan.
problems: The host line, format label, chapter label and illustration delay the actual question. Reduce the host line to one line and tighten the label-to-question gap by 8px.
The tilted shard bullets resemble stray marks rather than controls. Replace them with consistent outlined selection circles that fill when chosen.

screens.name: reply card
strengths: Removing the enclosing thread box lets the conversation breathe.
Sender labels, avatars and bubbles communicate the format without an explanation.
problems: The scenario setup dominates the conversation it introduces. Set the setup at 21px with a tighter line height so the thread becomes the visual center.
The selected answer differs mainly through a thin violet outline and pale fill. Add a visible checkmark and a stronger selected fill while preserving the text contrast.

screens.name: receipts card
strengths: The torn paper, rules and total turn a checklist into a convincing little game object.
Checkboxes and “Tear it off” clearly distinguish selection from submission.
problems: The large question heading crowds the receipt and pushes the submission control close to the screen bottom. Reduce the heading to 25px and its bottom margin to 12px.
The empty-state submission button has ambiguous availability. Give its disabled state a clearly muted fill and label it “Pick receipts to tear off”; restore “Tear it off” after a selection.

screens.name: rank card
strengths: Numbered rows and FIRST/LAST labels establish the ranking direction clearly.
The confirmation button separates arranging the list from submitting it.
problems: The stacked chevrons and dots look like a combined stepper and drag control. Use a simple six-dot drag handle and put accessible move-up/move-down controls in its focus state.
The fourth row is substantially taller, disrupting the list’s rhythm. Shorten it to “Appointments on weekdays. Weekends are mine” so all rows fit two lines.

screens.name: late-run card
strengths: The evolved Genii gives the late game a visible sense of progression.
The fitted-sheet detail makes the scenario unusually vivid and amusing.
problems: The five-line serif question makes this quick card feel heavy. Reduce the question size to 24px and tighten the line height to approximately 1.15.
The home illustration is mostly relegated beneath the card while its thumbnail repeats above. Reduce the lower illustration’s opacity and keep the upper thumbnail as the primary chapter cue.

screens.name: lock
strengths: The deep violet transition and completed mirror create a convincing moment of consequence.
The numbered explanation makes the prediction-and-play sequence understandable.
problems: The lock notice combines answer locking and Genii passing in one dense block. Keep “Your chapter answers lock next” in the notice and move the passing explanation into a short caption.
The CTA repeats “Genii’s guesses” after a large explanatory section. Shorten it to “Lock the 8 guesses” and retain the lock icon.

screens.name: two archetypes
strengths: The split stained-glass mirror is the set’s strongest identity reveal.
People-versus-life labels make the two-archetype concept legible without technical explanation.
problems: “The Go-Getter” breaks at the hyphen, making the archetype look squeezed into its compartment. Reduce that title slightly so it reads “The” above “Go-Getter.”
The Next control is faint and detached in a large empty footer. Increase its contrast and move it upward into a consistent bottom navigation position.

screens.name: your map
strengths: Separate stat-name rows now give the six measures a predictable reading order.
Fixed center ticks and highlighted endpoint labels make each direction easier to interpret.
problems: The glossy tracks and floating knobs still resemble adjustable sliders. Use flat tracks and smaller solid markers, and add “Your answers placed you here” beneath the subtitle.
Background sparkles and outlined shards interfere with the fine tracks and labels. Add a dark translucent backing behind the entire stats area and reduce nearby particle opacity.

screens.name: what Genii knows best
strengths: The featured finding followed by smaller findings provides a clear starting point.
Signal words improve the distinction between stronger and less decisive readings.
problems: The smaller cards cram stat name, result name and signal badge into competing positions on one row. Use a fixed layout: stat label above, result title below, signal badge at the upper right.
Six cards, repeated gem icons and multiple serif paragraphs create a dense wall. Show the strongest three findings here and move the remaining three behind a “See all six” disclosure.

screens.name: room by room
strengths: The light palette gives the reveal a useful visual reset.
Chapter islands connect abstract results to recognizable parts of everyday life.
problems: Result badges crowd the room titles, especially “With money.” Put each badge below its title and align the descriptions to a shared text column.

“Without you, the holidays would quietly fall apart” is much more absolute than the other descriptions. Change it to “You’re often the one keeping holiday traditions alive” to retain personality without overreaching.

screens.name: Genii's calls
strengths: Equal-height tiles give the eight outcomes a substantially cleaner structure.
The large 5-of-8 result and expressive Genii make the outcome emotionally readable.
problems: “Called it,” “Same side” and “Surprised Genii” require a bottom key that arrives after the grid. Move a compact three-status key directly above the tiles and include the missing “Surprised” definition.
The fracture lines on missed calls cross the tiles like accidental scratches. Confine the fracture treatment to the status icon and leave the title area clean.

screens.name: share card
strengths: Story/Post and Night/Day offer useful, understandable export choices.
The two-archetype mirror gives the shared image a recognizable branded silhouette.
problems: The exported card squeezes “The Go-Getter” against the mirror edges and makes the trait pills tiny. Reduce archetype type by 10% and enlarge the trait text within a wider footer area.

The preview, two segmented controls, three actions and two italic pitches compete for attention. Keep Share image dominant, move Copy link beside the friend action, and remove the opposite-archetype pitch from this screen.

screens.name: get the app
strengths: The lunch-to-island illustration gives the app handoff a concrete visual premise.
The dark App Store CTA stands out clearly against the luminous violet background.
problems: The illustration demonstrates lunch, but the description broadens into a vague “moment of your day.” Tie the copy to the image: “Snap your lunch. Miia lives it on your island, with Genii nearby.”
The large friend button competes with the install action directly beneath it. Convert “Do you really know me?” into a smaller text link and increase separation from the App Store button.

top_fixes: Rebuild screen 12’s small finding headers with fixed positions for stat, result and signal; show three findings initially and disclose the rest.
On screen 15, reduce archetype text by 10%, widen the trait footer and remove the opposite-archetype paragraph so the preview and Share image action dominate.
On screen 11, replace glossy slider tracks with flat tracks and smaller solid markers; add “Your answers placed you here” and suppress background particles behind the stats.
On screen 14, move a three-status legend above the grid and remove fracture lines from tile title areas.
On screen 2, add an explicit Continue action and a checkmark on the selected voice option.
Across question screens, shorten the host banner to one line and reduce question typography where it exceeds four lines; preserve answer text size and tap areas.
Remove reflected headline lettering on screens 1 and 3; reserve reflection effects for illustrated glass objects.
Fix screen 10’s Go-Getter line break and raise the Next control’s contrast; on screen 16, demote the friend action beneath the install CTA.
hooks: The set holds attention through specific scenarios, changing card formats and the accumulating mirror. The 12-screen reveal risks exhausting that momentum because several screens repeat the same conclusions. Screen 10 is the strongest screenshot moment: the split mirror makes the two-sided identity instantly tangible. Fix the Go-Getter line break, simplify the overlapping insight plaque and give the composition more breathing room to make it a stronger shareable reveal.
brand_fit: The violet glass, floating islands, shard progression and evolving droplet strongly fit the stated world. Genii reads as a glass slime, with a coherent orb-to-character progression. The main gap is restraint: repeated glows, translucent panels, serif blocks and background particles make the shell feel overdecorated. The illustrated world is distinctive; the information surfaces need cleaner contrast and a more disciplined type hierarchy to reach award-level craft.

meta.judge: Codex CLI, read-only, ephemeral, same 16-screen list and prompt shape as R3
meta.prompt_note: the second-pass prompt listed R3 and first-pass scores and named the changes made between passes
meta.screens_after_judging: after this verdict the knows-best rows moved the end into the line with a fixed header, the calls key moved above the tiles, cracks left the tile titles and long stat ends fill the footer alone (not re-judged)
